question: The total female literacy in India as per the 2011 census was ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**65.46%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the 2011 census, India's female literacy rate stood at **65.46%**, while the overall literacy rate for the country was **recorded at 74.4%**, with **males having a literacy rate of **82.14 **%**.
 
• Over the years, there has been a significant increase in literacy rates nationwide, rising from 18.33% in 1951 to 65.38% in 2001. During this period, male literacy rates were higher at 75.85% compared to female literacy rates at 54.16%.
 
• Among the states in India, Kerala boasted the highest literacy rate in 2011, reaching 94%.
 
• Following Kerala were Chandigarh, Himachal Pradesh, and the capital territory of Delhi, all with literacy rates above the national average. Interestingly, despite leading in literacy, all these states reported higher literacy rates among males than females.
 
• Additionally, the Jain community emerged as the most literate community in India, reflecting their significant emphasis on education and learning.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The 2011 census of India,** also known as the 15th Indian census, was conducted in two phases: house listing and population enumeration.
 
• Commencing on April 1, 2010, the house listing phase focused on gathering information about all buildings.
 
• Additionally, this phase included the collection of data for the National Population Register (NPR), which aims to provide a 12-digit unique identification number to all registered Indian residents.
 
• This identification number will be issued by the Unique Identification Authority of India, utilizing the information collected during the house listing phase.
